Closed thin rock edge with grounded base, no floating relief or visible open seam. Edge-on view cannot establish branching and is not used to claim it.
Slab thickness and long profile remain unchanged at the intended scale; no tall living frond or separate underside appears.
Closed opposite slab edge. No new layered-skin artifact visible in this fixed frame.

Clear tapering frond envelope, staggered broad primary units meeting at the central zigzag boundary, and shorter gently curved nearly longitudinal secondary grooves inside those units. Middle and lower interior units now resolve as nested regions rather than the former isolated diagonal slash facets. Finest apical divisions naturally merge at 512 pixels; no claim of every tiny branch being resolved.
The same subordinate relief remains visible without the darker impression palette. The oblique clay view is weaker than the neutral-gray top, but does not collapse to the former near-flat patch.
Rounded slab end corners match the original rounded outline. This is rock outline evidence, not proof of fossil branch recognition.
